title: Louisiana GOP Moves to Erase Majority-Black Districts
excerpt: A Supreme Court ruling gutting the Voting Rights Act hands Republicans the power to redraw — and potentially eliminate — both of Louisiana's Black-majority seats.
body:
Louisiana Republicans opened an eight-hour state senate hearing on May 9, 2026, proposing to dismantle at least one — and possibly both — of the state's majority-Black congressional districts, setting off one of the most charged redistricting battles in the American South in decades.

**What the Supreme Court unleashed:**
On April 29, 2026, a 6-3 Supreme Court majority struck down Louisiana's 2024 congressional map in *Louisiana v. Callais*, ruling that the intentional creation of a second majority-Black district was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander. The decision, authored by Justice Samuel Alito, significantly weakened Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. Justice Elena Kagan wrote in dissent that the ruling renders Section 2 'all but a dead letter.' Governor Jeff Landry moved swiftly, postponing U.S. House primaries scheduled for May 16 — even though tens of thousands of ballots had already been mailed.

**A redistricting arms race across the South:**
Louisiana is now the epicenter of a broader Republican push. State Senator Jay Morris put forward plans that would hand Republicans five or all six of the state's U.S. House seats — erasing both Democratic-held, majority-Black districts entirely. Black voters make up one-third of Louisiana's electorate but currently hold only two of six seats. Similar moves are underway in Tennessee, Alabama, and South Carolina. Across the hearing room, civil rights leaders invoked the movement's history, warning that the new map would mark a return to state-sponsored racial discrimination.

**What to watch:**
Louisiana's senate is expected to unveil a formal new congressional map by mid-May; the final version will signal whether Republicans pursue a 5-1 or 6-0 partisan sweep — a decision that could tilt the national House balance ahead of November midterms.
